name: Bensen B-8M Gyrocopter
notes: Source: CLAUDE.md. Speeds entered as knots, stored in m/s.
Speeds from vortechonline.com Bensen B-8M page (cruise 65 mph, max 95 mph), converted to knots (x 0.869), rounded down.
Rated rpm 4100 and direct drive are assumptions for the McCulloch 4318; confirm in Stage 6.
Rotor rpm: 200 minimum for take-off, 400 maximum (user supplied).
Take-off roll 30 m assumes prerotation. Brakes TBC in Stage 6.
Gear and inertia are Stage 3 engineering estimates, to be refined in Stage 6.
Gear: foot-steered nosewheel (+/-34 deg) 1.5 m ahead of CG, mains 0.25 m behind CG on a 1.5 m axle, small keel tail skid; sits level.
Inertia is the airframe only (pilot, engine, keel); rotor inertia is modelled separately in Stage 6.
Stage 6 flight model (estimates tuned to the CLAUDE.md targets; see docs/STATUS.md):

Rotor: 2-blade teetering, 7 in (0.178 m) chord, solidity 0.037, NACA 8-H-12 type blades (lift slope 5.7/rad, profile drag 0.011), fixed pitch 5.5 deg (sets ~360-370 rpm in cruise), ~60 kg m2. Head tilted back 2.5 deg at neutral stick (trims about 50 kt hands-off), 12 deg forward and 20 deg back (to load the rotor on the take-off roll), +/-7 deg roll.

Prerotator: clutch from the engine, 140 N m at the rotor, drives up to 330 rpm (near flight rpm, needed for the CLAUDE.md 30 m take-off roll). The clutch passes full torque from 2,600 engine rpm and less towards idle, so it cannot stall the engine.
Propeller: 52 x 22 in wooden pusher, direct drive, about 150 kgf static thrust, thrust line 0.18 m above the CG (nose-down moment with power: the power-pushover hazard).

Airframe: open frame with pilot, drag area 0.6 m2 (sets the 82 kt top speed); fin and rudder (0.45 m2) in the slipstream; small tailplane (0.15 m2, assumed: the stock B-8M had none; this small one keeps pitch lively, so a sharp pushover really does unload the rotor).
Cruise (decided 2026-10-19): the Bensen 65 mph (56 kt) cruise is level flight at about 45% power (~3,500 rpm); full power gives the 82 kt maximum.
Engine: McCulloch 4318, 65 hp at 4100 rpm, two-stroke flat four, direct drive (assumed); bsfc 0.5 kg/kWh.

Hands-off trim (user request 2026-10-19): head rigged 0.95 deg back and 1.6 deg right (cancels propeller torque at cruise power), fin offset 0.5 deg (cancels propeller yaw), plus stick-free roll stability that keeps the rotor disc level when the stick is released sideways (modern-gyro behaviour; the stock B-8M was spirally neutral). Hands-off at 45% power it flies straight and level at 53 kt with about a 1 deg left-wing-low list; power changes climb or descend.

Roll and pitch damping (2026-10-20, user: roll too aggressive): the disc lag is the blade flapping time constant 16/(Lock number x rotor speed), Lock number about 3.7 from the blade data (rotor inertia 60 kg m2 over 2 blades), about 0.11 s at 370 rpm. The earlier fixed 0.04 s gave ~165 deg/s at full stick; now about 60 deg/s.

Brakes on all three wheels (user request 2026-10-19; assumed, the stock B-8M had none): main brakes alone (about 60% of the weight) slipped above ~2,800 engine rpm; with the nosewheel braked too the gyro holds still while prerotating at ~2,800 rpm on gravel and ~2,500 rpm on grass.
